title: Region-aware tiered routing with hosted contingency and safe model-variant fallback
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: We need a single policy framework that decides region selection and tier routing for incoming inference requests and safely spills over to hosted capacity when dedicated pools are constrained. This must also include deterministic, auditable fallback to compatible model variants (quantized/low-memory) without regressing critical SLAs or customer data residency constraints.

Goals:
- Ensure tenant requests route to the correct region and capacity tier by policy (region affinity, tenant residency, subscription tier).
- Provide predictable spillover to hosted endpoints with throttles and prioritization so Dedicated outages don't cascade into platform instability.
- Automate safe fallback to model variants (e.g., fp16 -> 8-bit quantized or smaller architecture) with quality guardrails and automatic rollback if quality regressions are detected.
- Maintain observability and an ops playbook to handle degradations and to keep per-tenant SLOs transparent.

Scope:
- Routing decision layer changes (policy DSL + enforcement hooks)
- Capacity signals (Dedicated pool utilization, queue lengths, GPU load, KV cache hit rates) to be consumed by router
- Spillover control plane for hosted invocation including rate-limits, per-tenant quotas, and per-model compatibility mapping
- Fallback variant registry and validation checks (model compatibility matrix, tokenization checks, structured output compatibility)

Out of scope for this ticket: billing integration for spillover, full RBAC expose in Console (will follow in PM-46023).
acceptance_criteria: Router applies region affinity and tenant residency rules for >95% of requests in simulation traces
When Dedicated pool >= 90% GPU utilization, new requests are selectively throttled and spillover begins per policy without exceeding hosted QPS budgets
Fallback to quantized variant is opt-in per tenant and requires passing a lightweight prompt-sanity test before traffic is routed
Observability: per-tenant dashboard shows routing decisions, spillover count, and fallback activations with links to traces
Playbook exists and is linked in comments; on-call can trigger immediate fallback rollback within 2 minutes
comments: 2026-02-26 - Asha K: Initial design doc posted. See Confluence link. Requesting feedback from SRE and Runtime teams.

2026-03-02 - Marco R: Ran a 24h synthetic traffic sim with region skew (60% EU, 30% NA, 10% APAC). Router honored residency for 99.1% but triggered spillover at the expected threshold. Observed higher KV cache miss rate for spilled requests — potential cost trade-off.
2026-03-04 - SRE (Riley Chen): Suggest adding a circuit-breaker that enforces a hard cap on hosted spillover per-region to prevent cross-region overload during progressive failure modes.
2026-03-05 - PM (Lina Ortega): Important to surface 'data residency' flag in decision logs for audit — legal requested this for EEA customers.
2026-03-08 - Design (Priya Menon): UX request to add a per-tenant toggle in Console for 'allow fallback variants' and a small explainer about potential QoE changes.

2026-03-10 - Marco R: Prototype implementation pushed: github.com/redwood-inference/route-engine/pull/812. Includes policy DSL parser and a simulation harness. Need review on compatibility matrix storage design.
2026-03-11 - Security (Jon Park): Confirmed fallback variant metadata must be signed and recorded to prevent tampering for Private deployments. Marked security_review_required=true.

2026-03-12 - Marco R: Performance smoke test results: end-to-end median latency increased ~18ms for spilled requests due to cross-region hops; plan to mitigate with regional caches and pre-warmed hosted slots.
notes: Trade-offs: allowing aggressive spillover reduces request rejection but raises cost and increases latency for affected tenants. Fallback variants reduce memory and latency but risk semantic drift — we'll gate fallback with per-tenant eval prompts and a QC pipeline. Next steps: finalize policy DSL, integrate capacity signals (ENG-21473), and implement Console toggle (PM-46023).
